title: Al-Maajid, the Noble
tomorrow: Al-Wahid, the One. one what, exactly?

cards: Splitting the check. One friend always reaches for it first; another always seems to have forgotten a wallet. Without saying so, people keep score of who gives.
The Prophet, peace be upon him, settled the question of the two hands in one line: the upper hand is better than the lower hand. The upper hand is the one that gives; the lower is the one that asks.
Today's Name puts that in God's own terms. Al-Maajid, the Noble, glorious in generosity.

teach.h: GLORY SHOWS UP AS A GIFT.
teach.b: One question today: what makes someone noble? In the Qur'an, glory shows up as a gift.

Angels bring Abraham's household news of a son in old age, his wife laughs, and they answer, in Pickthall's words: "Lo! He is Owner of Praise, Owner of Glory!" God's glory, in that scene, is generosity to an old couple.
So for people, noble isn't a title or a family name.

teach.h: THE UPPER HAND, BEGINNING AT HOME.
teach.b: It's the upper hand. And the same hadith adds two practical lines: begin with those you're responsible for, and the best charity comes from what's beyond your own needs.
Here's where a neighbor tradition sounds very close.

In the Bible's book of Acts, Paul tells a group of church elders to remember "the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive." Shared, then: the giving hand is the honored one.
A church meal train and a Muslim's sadaqa look alike from across the table. And one honest difference.
In Islam, one kind of giving, zakat, is a pillar, a duty with its own rules, named in the hadith that says Islam is built on five.
Churches each have their own ways with giving, and the line in Acts speaks of blessing, not a fixed share. Two traditions, each in its own words.
The giving hand is noble in both.

how: Muslims give zakat, a required share of wealth, and sadaqa, charity given freely, beginning with family and those in need nearby; Al-Maajid is called on among the Names.

o: the Proud, who stands apart from all
the Royal, born above everyone else

games.q: two hands, two traditions — tap the pairs.
p: more blessed to give than to receive
a pillar: giving with set rules

s: in the hadith, the upper hand is the one that gives
the upper hand is better than the lower hand: the giver's over the asker's.
'It is more blessed to give than to receive' comes from the Qur'an
it's in the Bible, Acts 20:35, given as words of the Lord Jesus. the Prophet's 'upper hand' saying sounds close to it.
noble means born into an important family
in the Qur'an's scene, glory shows up as generosity: a son promised to an old couple.

games.q: you win $100 in a school contest. your little brother needs new cleats, and a classmate is raising money for a shelter. what does the 'upper hand' hadith say to do first?
o: give it all to the shelter; strangers count most.
start with the one you're responsible for, then give from what's left over.
keep it; you earned it, and charity is for adults.
games.why: the hadith that praises the upper hand also says: begin with your dependents, and the best charity is from what's beyond your needs. cleats first, then the shelter.

practice: Choose one act only the upper hand can do: pay for someone's coffee, give credit out loud to the person who earned it, hand over the last slice. Plan it now in detail: who, when, how.
Then sit with the plan for the two minutes, quietly, since noble doesn't need an audience.

wordCard.voice: Al-Maajid. The Noble: glory that shows itself by giving, Owner of Praise, Owner of Glory.

orig.note: Arabic: the Noble, glorious in generosity. a close form, majid, 'Owner of Glory', is in Surah Hud.

carryVoice: The one to keep: noble, the hand that gives without keeping any score. Good night.

sources.q: Lo! He is Owner of Praise, Owner of Glory!

sources.ref: Qur'an 11:69–73 (angels bring Abraham's household news of a son; his wife laughs)

sources.q: the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 1427, 1429 (the upper hand is better than the lower; begin with your dependents; the best charity is from what is beyond your needs)
Sahih al-Bukhari 8 (Islam is built on five, including zakat)
